chunks: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said:
“Indeed, when the nails are affected by al-nūrah, it changes them until they resemble the nails of the dead, so there is no harm in changing them.”

key_terms.أَظَافِيرَ الْمَوْتَى: the nails of the deceased, used here as a comparison in appearance
key_terms.النُّورَةُ: depilatory paste that affects the nails' appearance
key_terms.الْأَظَافِيرَ: the fingernails or nails being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.بِتَغْيِيرِهَا: in changing them or altering their appearance
key_terms.تُشْبِهُ: comes to resemble or look like
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it indicates permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to change the appearance of nails after they are affected by al-nūrah?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir عليه السلام states that when nails are altered by al-nūrah and take on an appearance like the nails of the deceased, changing that appearance is permissible. The hadith conveys a practical legal allowance related to cleanliness and bodily grooming.
